deck: OET — z ćwiczeń (Reading, Listening, Writing, Speaking)

notes.example:
A compound fracture of the tibia was confirmed on X-ray, and the patient was taken to theatre for washout.
With a compound fracture the bone breaks through the skin, so infection is a major risk.
He sustained a compound fracture of the forearm when he fell from the ladder.

notes.back: złamanie typu buckle (torus) — wgniecenie warstwy korowej kości
notes.example:
A buckle fracture of the distal radius is common in children who fall onto an outstretched hand.
The X-ray showed a buckle fracture, so a removable splint was applied rather than a full cast.
Buckle fractures are usually stable and tend to heal well with simple immobilisation.

She sustained an ankle sprain while playing netball.
A grade two sprain involves a partial tear of the ligament.
Most mild sprains settle within two weeks with rest, ice and elevation.

Direct pressure is the first step to halt haemorrhage from a wound.
The surgeon placed a suture to halt haemorrhage from the vessel.
A tourniquet may be needed to halt haemorrhage when pressure alone fails.
notes.synonyms: to stop bleeding / to control bleeding / to staunch bleeding

notes.example:
A pressure bandage was applied over the wound to control the bleeding.
Apply a pressure bandage firmly, but check that the toes remain warm and pink.
The pressure bandage should be left in place until the patient is reviewed by a doctor.

The paramedics immobilised the cervical spine before moving the patient.
It is important to immobilise the limb to prevent further damage.
We need to immobilise the wrist in a splint for several weeks.
notes.synonyms: to keep still / to splint / to secure in place

notes.example:
A plaster backslab was applied to the leg to allow for swelling.
He went home in a plaster backslab and was asked to return to the fracture clinic in a week.
The plaster backslab should be kept dry and must not be removed.

Her arm was placed in a sling for comfort.
He should wear the sling for two weeks and then start gentle movement.
The nurse showed the patient how to adjust the sling so that the wrist is supported.

Elevate the limb above the level of the heart to reduce swelling.
Patients are advised to elevate the leg whenever they are sitting.
The nurse helped him to elevate the injured arm on two pillows.
notes.synonyms: to raise / to lift / to prop up

notes.example:
He described a throbbing pain in the left thigh that was worse at night.
The throbbing headache was accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light.
Is the pain throbbing, stabbing or aching?

Capillary refill was under two seconds and peripheral pulses palpable distal to the injury.
On examination: warm, well perfused, peripheral pulses palpable.
Peripheral pulses palpable bilaterally; no sensory deficit.

Severe pain out of proportion to the injury should raise suspicion of compartment syndrome.
Compartment syndrome is a surgical emergency that may require fasciotomy.
After the tibial fracture he developed compartment syndrome and was taken to theatre urgently.
notes.synonyms: raised pressure within a muscle compartment

notes.example:
The dose was increased in increments of 2.5 mg every three days.
Morphine can be titrated in small increments until the pain is controlled.
Please increase the infusion rate in increments of 10 mL per hour.

Pad the bony prominences, such as the heel and the elbow, before applying the plaster.
Pressure ulcers tend to develop over bony prominences like the sacrum.
Check the bony prominences daily for redness or breakdown of the skin.
notes.synonyms: areas where bone lies close to the skin

notes.example:
A crepe bandage was wrapped firmly around the ankle to support the sprain.
Apply the crepe bandage from the toes upwards, overlapping each turn by half.
Remove the crepe bandage at night and reapply it in the morning.

A layer of stockinette is placed on the skin before the padding and plaster.
The stockinette is rolled back over the edges of the cast to give a smooth finish.
She was fitted with a stockinette liner before the cast was applied.
notes.synonyms: tubular cotton liner worn under a cast

notes.example:
Please read the Consumer Medicine Information that comes with your tablets.
The pharmacist gave her the Consumer Medicine Information and went through the main side effects.
If you are unsure how to take the medicine, check the Consumer Medicine Information first.

Some pacemakers are susceptible to interference from strong magnetic fields.
Wireless monitors may be susceptible to interference from other electronic devices.
Older hearing aids can be susceptible to interference from mobile phones.

The tumour lies in close proximity to the spinal cord, which makes surgery difficult.
Patients with infectious diarrhoea should not be nursed in close proximity to other patients.
The clinic is located in close proximity to the main hospital.
notes.synonyms: very close to / right next to / adjacent to

notes.example:
Displacement of the feeding tube was suspected when the patient coughed after the feed.
Tube displacement is a common complication in confused patients.
Check for displacement of the tube before each feed by confirming the marked length.

Regurgitation of food after meals can lead to aspiration in patients with a feeding tube.
The baby had frequent regurgitation after feeds but was gaining weight well.
Raising the head of the bed can reduce regurgitation during enteral feeding.

Aspiration of stomach contents is a serious risk in patients with a reduced level of consciousness.
The speech therapist assessed her swallow because of the risk of aspiration.
Sit the patient upright during feeding to reduce the risk of aspiration.
notes.synonyms: inhaling food or fluid into the lungs

notes.example:
Staff must have their competency assessed before they are allowed to change the dressings alone.
All nurses who insert the tubes must have their competency assessed before working unsupervised.
Competency assessed and signed off by the ward manager on 3 March.
notes.synonyms: formally checked as able to do the task

notes.example:
All new staff must complete mandatory training in infection control within their first week.
Fire safety is part of the annual mandatory training.
She was unable to work on the ward until her mandatory training was up to date.

The doctor offered the patient a chaperone before the examination.
A chaperone should be present during any intimate examination.
She declined a chaperone, and this was recorded in the notes.
notes.synonyms: a person present during an intimate examination

notes.example:
A nurse acted as a formal chaperone during the breast examination.
The practice policy is to provide a formal chaperone for every intimate examination.
A formal chaperone has been trained for the role and records their presence in the notes.

The patient chose her sister as an informal chaperone.
An informal chaperone, such as a friend or relative, can provide comfort but is not trained for the role.
He asked his wife to stay as an informal chaperone during the examination.
notes.synonyms: relative or friend who stays in the room

notes.example:
The patient decided to decline an offer of a chaperone.
She chose to decline an offer of further tests until she had spoken to her family.
It is her right to decline an offer of treatment, provided she understands the risks.
notes.synonyms: to turn down an offer / to refuse politely

notes.example:
The pharmacist carries out spot checks on the controlled drugs cupboard every month.
Spot checks of hand hygiene are carried out on all wards.
Managers use spot checks to confirm that staff follow the protocol.

The incidence of type 2 diabetes has risen sharply over the past thirty years.
The incidence of wound infection was 4% in the treatment group.
Incidence refers to new cases arising in a given period, whereas prevalence refers to all existing cases.

This retrospective multi-centre study reviewed the records of 2,400 patients treated between 2015 and 2020.
A retrospective multi-centre study cannot prove causation, because the data were not collected for the research.
The authors carried out a retrospective multi-centre study across eight UK hospitals.

Myriad factors influence whether a patient takes their medication as prescribed.
There are myriad reasons why people delay seeking help for low mood.
The patient presented with a myriad of vague symptoms that were difficult to link.

Cognitive impairment can make it difficult for patients to follow medication instructions.
Hearing impairment is common in older adults and often goes unrecognised.
The stroke left her with a mild visual impairment.
notes.synonyms: reduced function / deficit / loss of ability

notes.example:
A common refrain among shift workers is that they never feel fully rested.
"I don't have time to exercise" is a common refrain in clinic.
A common refrain from patients is that nobody explained the diagnosis to them.
notes.synonyms: something people say again and again

notes.example:
Blood pressure is not the be-all and end-all when assessing cardiovascular risk.
For some patients, weight loss becomes the be-all and end-all of the consultation.
A single test result should not be the be-all and end-all of the diagnosis.
notes.synonyms: the only thing that matters / the most important factor

notes.example:
Shift workers can build up a sleep debt over a run of night shifts.
A weekend of lie-ins does not fully repay a sleep debt.
Chronic sleep debt is associated with poor concentration and low mood.

The onset of symptoms was sudden, with severe chest pain at rest.

Can you tell me about the onset of the pain? Was it sudden or gradual?

The disease trajectory varies considerably between patients.

Frailty can alter the trajectory of recovery after surgery.

The prevalence of obesity among children has doubled in twenty years.
Prevalence is higher in women than in men.
The study estimated the prevalence of depression at 12% in the over-seventies.
notes.synonyms: proportion of people affected at one time

notes.example:
A viral trigger is a plausible explanation for her symptoms.
The mechanism seems biologically plausible, but it has not been proven.
His account of the fall was plausible, but the injuries suggested otherwise.

Stringent infection control measures were introduced on the ward.
The trial applied stringent inclusion criteria, so the results may not apply to all patients.
Drug storage is subject to stringent rules.

Many patients have sub-threshold symptoms that still cause distress.
A sub-threshold dose had no measurable effect on blood pressure.
She had sub-threshold anxiety, which did not meet the criteria for a disorder.

The programme provides scaffolding for patients who are learning to manage their condition.
Regular appointments offered the scaffolding she needed to stay in treatment.
Family support can act as scaffolding during the first months of recovery.

The explanation proffered by the patient did not match the pattern of her injuries.
He declined the advice proffered by the nurse.
Several theories have been proffered to account for the rise in cases.

The conflicting results have fuelled questions about the safety of the drug.
Delays in diagnosis continue to fuel questions about the quality of care.
The report is likely to fuel questions about staffing levels.
notes.synonyms: to raise doubts / to prompt further debate

notes.example:
Rheumatoid arthritis afflicts around one per cent of the population.
A range of health problems afflict people who live in poor housing.
He was afflicted by chronic back pain for most of his working life.
notes.synonyms: to affect / to trouble / to plague

notes.example:
She has had sciatica for three weeks, with pain shooting down the left leg.
Sciatica is often caused by a prolapsed disc pressing on a nerve root.
Most cases of sciatica improve within six to twelve weeks without surgery.
notes.synonyms: pain running down the leg from the lower back

notes.example:
The aim of treatment is to prevent recurrence of the ulcer.
Recurrence is common in the first year after stopping the medication.
Is there a risk of recurrence after the operation?

Spinal manipulation may give short-term relief for lower back pain.
The physiotherapist performed manipulation of the lower back, and the stiffness improved.
Manipulation is not appropriate when there are red flag symptoms such as numbness around the groin.
notes.synonyms: hands-on treatment of the spine or joints

notes.example:
A pigmented lesion on her back had changed in size and colour.
The CT scan showed a solitary lesion in the right lobe of the liver.
Lesions on the legs were weeping and crusted.
notes.synonyms: abnormal area of tissue / patch / growth

notes.example:
Neglected diseases mainly affect people in the poorest regions of the world.
Schistosomiasis is classed as a neglected disease because it attracts little investment.
Control programmes for neglected diseases rely heavily on donated medicines.
notes.synonyms: illness that receives little research funding

notes.example:
She attended her first ante-natal appointment at ten weeks.
Ante-natal classes cover labour, breastfeeding and caring for a newborn.
All pregnant women are offered ante-natal screening for anaemia.

Post-natal depression can develop within the first year after delivery.
She was invited for a post-natal check six weeks after the birth.
The midwife visits the mother at home during the post-natal period.

She went into labour at 38 weeks and was admitted to the delivery suite.
The first stage of labour can last many hours in a first pregnancy.
Labour was induced because the pregnancy had continued beyond 41 weeks.

Dispensing medication is carried out by the pharmacist in line with the prescription.
The pharmacy technician is responsible for dispensing medication in the outpatient department.
Errors in dispensing medication can cause serious harm.

The fracture healed in a misaligned position and needed surgical correction.
A misaligned tooth was causing ulceration on her cheek.
The X-ray showed that the bones were slightly misaligned.
notes.synonyms: out of position / not properly lined up

notes.example:
Setbacks are common in rehabilitation, so it is important to stay positive.
He suffered a few setbacks during recovery, including a chest infection.
Please don't be discouraged by minor setbacks; progress is rarely a straight line.

It can take time to come to terms with a diagnosis of diabetes.
She is trying to come to terms with the loss of her independence.
Counselling can help families come to terms with the news.
notes.synonyms: to accept / to adjust to / to learn to live with

notes.example:
He reports a two-month history of dysphagia, worse with solids than with liquids.
Progressive dysphagia to solids should prompt urgent investigation for oesophageal cancer.
The patient complained of dysphagia when eating bread and meat.

She has had a post-viral cough for six weeks.
Post-viral fatigue usually improves gradually over weeks to months.
The patient developed a post-viral arthritis that resolved without treatment.

He has been taking over-the-counter ibuprofen for the pain.

She occasionally uses an over-the-counter antihistamine for hay fever.

notes.example:
My provisional diagnosis is a migraine, but I would like to exclude other causes.

notes.synonyms: working diagnosis / initial diagnosis / tentative diagnosis

notes.example:
A biopsy is needed to establish a definitive diagnosis.
Until a definitive diagnosis is made, we will treat the symptoms.

Symptoms ceased within an hour of starting treatment.
notes.synonyms: to stop / to discontinue / to halt

notes.example:
He is a social drinker and does not smoke.

The patient is a social drinker; there is no history of alcohol dependence.
notes.synonyms: someone who drinks alcohol only occasionally

notes.example:
She had a tonsillectomy at the age of seven after recurrent tonsillitis.

A small sebaceous cyst was noted on the back of the neck.

notes.synonyms: lump under the skin filled with oily material

notes.example:
He developed a whiplash injury after a rear-end collision.

notes.synonyms: neck sprain after a sudden jolt

notes.example:
Fatigue is one of the most common reasons patients visit their GP.
Since the infection she has been struggling with extreme fatigue.
Does the fatigue get worse as the day goes on?

You will probably be discharged from hospital on Friday.
Before you are discharged, the pharmacist will go through your medicines.
She was discharged from hospital two days after the operation.

How is your exercise tolerance? Can you still climb the stairs without stopping?
notes.synonyms: how much activity someone can manage

notes.example:
I would like to refer you to a cardiac rehabilitation programme.

We can discuss a phased return to work with your employer.

Try to eat more whole grains, such as oats, brown rice and wholemeal bread.

notes.synonyms: steps / precautions / moves to deal with a situation

notes.example:
Handwashing is one of the most effective preventive measures against infection.

notes.synonyms: precautions / steps to stop it happening

notes.example:
Safety measures such as non-slip flooring and good lighting reduce the risk of falls.
The ward follows strict safety measures when handling cytotoxic drugs.

The primary outcome measures were mortality and length of hospital stay.

Patient-reported outcome measures help clinicians understand how treatment affects daily life.
notes.synonyms: ways of assessing the result of treatment

notes.back: radzić sobie z problemem, zarządzać problemem (nie: „manage with”)
notes.example:
Patients are taught how to manage a problem such as breathlessness at home.

notes.synonyms: to deal with a problem / to handle an issue

notes.example:
Many patients find it hard to cope with chronic pain.
